title: An exact equivalence induces an equivalence on bounded below derived categories
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] and let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ be exact additive functors (they preserve short exact sequences and addition on morphisms) with natural isomorphisms $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\cong GF$ and $FG\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$ making them quasi-inverse equivalences. Applying $F$ and $G$ termwise to cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] induces quasi-inverse equivalences
$$F^+:D^+(\mathcal A)\ \simeq\ D^+(\mathcal B):G^+.$$
The derived functors carry the given unit and counit to their termwise induced natural isomorphisms. In particular $F^+$ and $G^+$ preserve and reflect isomorphisms. Here $D^+$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] is the full subcategory of the derived category on objects with cohomology zero in all sufficiently negative degrees.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, applied to quasi-inverse exact functors; formal consequence for equivalences, used in the perfect-closure reduction of the field-extension lemma

proof.text: Write $C(F)$ and $C(G)$ for termwise application to cochain complexes, and $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ for the localization functors. The equivalence of the two descriptions of exactness in [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] puts the given additive short-exact-sequence-preserving functors under the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Apply that statement to $F$ and $G$. Thus $C(F)$ and $C(G)$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms, and there are functors $F_D:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ and $G_D:D(\mathcal B)\to D(\mathcal A)$ with natural isomorphisms $\phi^F_K:F_DQ_{\mathcal A}K\to Q_{\mathcal B}C(F)K$ and $\phi^G_L:G_DQ_{\mathcal B}L\to Q_{\mathcal A}C(G)L$. These are exactly the functors computed on any complex by termwise application; no injective objects or resolutions are assumed.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; formal localization argument for quasi-inverse exact functors, supplied here

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below] separately to $F$ and $G$. For every integer $a$, $F_D$ carries $D(\mathcal A)^{\ge a}$ into $D(\mathcal B)^{\ge a}$, and $G_D$ carries $D(\mathcal B)^{\ge a}$ into $D(\mathcal A)^{\ge a}$. By [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], each bounded below object belongs to one such subcategory, with a bound allowed to depend on the object. Restrict $F_D,G_D$ to the full subcategories to obtain $F^+:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathcal B)$ and $G^+:D^+(\mathcal B)\to D^+(\mathcal A)$. On morphisms these restrictions are the same functors, since the subcategories are full.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; formal localization argument for quasi-inverse exact functors, supplied here

proof.text: Let $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{\sim}GF$ and $\epsilon:FG\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal B}$ be the given unit and counit. Define $(\eta^C_K)^r=\eta_{K^r}$ and $(\epsilon^C_L)^r=\epsilon_{L^r}$. These are morphisms of the complexes of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: naturality at $d_K^r$ says $GF(d_K^r)\eta_{K^r}=\eta_{K^{r+1}}d_K^r$, and naturality of $\epsilon$ gives $d_L^r\epsilon_{L^r}=\epsilon_{L^{r+1}}FG(d_L^r)$. The degreewise inverses satisfy the reverse equations, and naturality at each component of a chain map gives naturality in $K,L$. Hence $\eta^C:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}C(G)C(F)$ and $\epsilon^C:C(F)C(G)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ are natural isomorphisms of functors on complexes.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; formal localization argument for quasi-inverse exact functors, supplied here

proof.text:
For each $K$, form the natural isomorphism $a_K=\phi^G_{C(F)K}\circ G_D(\phi^F_K):G_DF_DQ_{\mathcal A}K\to Q_{\mathcal A}C(G)C(F)K$. For each $L$, put $b_L=\phi^F_{C(G)L}\circ F_D(\phi^G_L):F_DG_DQ_{\mathcal B}L\to Q_{\mathcal B}C(F)C(G)L$. The factorizations in [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] give these identifications of the composites with their termwise models. Now $a^{-1}\circ Q_{\mathcal A}(\eta^C)$ is a natural isomorphism $Q_{\mathcal A}\to G_DF_DQ_{\mathcal A}$, and $Q_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon^C)\circ b$ is one from $F_DG_DQ_{\mathcal B}$ to $Q_{\mathcal B}$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to each localization, with these pairs of functors and identity comparison isomorphisms. All four functors before descent invert quasi-isomorphisms because they factor through $Q_{\mathcal A}$ or $Q_{\mathcal B}$. We obtain natural isomorphisms $\eta_D:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_DF_D$ and $\epsilon_D:F_DG_D\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$, characterized by
$$\eta_{D,Q_{\mathcal A}K}=a_K^{-1}Q_{\mathcal A}(\eta^C_K),\qquad \epsilon_{D,Q_{\mathcal B}L}=Q_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon^C_L)b_L.$$
Their inverses are the lifts of the inverse transformations, since lifting respects composition and identities. Thus the descended unit and counit are the given termwise ones under the displayed factorizations.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; formal localization argument for quasi-inverse exact functors, supplied here

proof.text: The unit and counit just constructed restrict to natural isomorphisms $\eta^+:\mathrm{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}G^+F^+$ and $\epsilon^+:F^+G^+\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$: all their endpoints lie in the bounded below subcategories by Step 2, and fullness in [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] includes both the components and their inverses. These isomorphisms exhibit the restrictions as quasi-inverses. If the given unit and counit are specified with the adjunction triangle identities, those identities descend as well. Indeed, after precomposition with $Q_{\mathcal A}$, the transformation $\epsilon_DF_D\circ F_D\eta_D$ becomes, using the Step 4 factorizations and their naturality, $Q_{\mathcal B}(\epsilon^C_{C(F)K}\circ C(F)(\eta^C_K))=Q_{\mathcal B}(\mathrm{id}_{C(F)K})$; the other composite becomes $Q_{\mathcal A}(C(G)(\epsilon^C_L)\circ\eta^C_{C(G)L})=Q_{\mathcal A}(\mathrm{id}_{C(G)L})$. These are the original triangle equations in each degree. Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] identifies the two composites with identity natural transformations on the derived categories, and restriction retains these equations.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; formal localization argument for quasi-inverse exact functors, supplied here

proof.text: Every functor preserves isomorphisms: apply it to the two inverse equations. To check reflection explicitly, let $u:X\to Y$ in $D^+(\mathcal A)$ and suppose $F^+(u)$ has inverse $t$. Set $v=(\eta^+_X)^{-1}\circ G^+(t)\circ\eta^+_Y:Y\to X$. Naturality gives $\eta^+_Y u=G^+F^+(u)\eta^+_X$, so $vu=\mathrm{id}_X$ by $tF^+(u)=\mathrm{id}$, and $uv=\mathrm{id}_Y$ by $F^+(u)t=\mathrm{id}$ and the same naturality equation solved for $u$. Hence $u$ is invertible. For a map $u:X\to Y$ in $D^+(\mathcal B)$ such that $G^+(u)$ has inverse $t$, the same calculation with the natural isomorphism $(\epsilon^+)^{-1}:\mathrm{id}\to F^+G^+$ gives the inverse $\epsilon^+_X\circ F^+(t)\circ(\epsilon^+_Y)^{-1}$. This proves preservation and reflection for both functors.

lean.statement: theorem exactEquivalenceDerivedPlus {A : Type u} {B : Type u'} [Category.{v} A] [Category.{v'} B] [Abelian A] [Abelian B] [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ A) [F.Additive] [G.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] [PreservesFiniteColimits G] (η : 𝟭 A ≅ F ⋙ G) (ε : G ⋙ F ≅ 𝟭 B) : let Fplus := F.mapDerivedCategoryPlus let Gplus := G.mapDerivedCategoryPlus let ηplus := (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusIdIso A).symm ≪≫ Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso η ≪≫ Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso F G let εplus := (Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusCompIso G F).symm ≪≫ Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusNatIso ε ≪≫ Functor.mapDerivedCategoryPlusIdIso B ∃ e : DerivedCategory.Plus A ≌ DerivedCategory.Plus B, e = Equivalence.mk Fplus Gplus ηplus εplus ∧ (∀ {X Y : DerivedCategory.Plus A} (f : X ⟶ Y), IsIso (Fplus.map f) ↔ IsIso f) ∧ (∀ {X Y : DerivedCategory.Plus B} (f : X ⟶ Y), IsIso (Gplus.map f) ↔ IsIso f)
